summary: Francis N. J. specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a Master's in Ancient History from the University of Calicut and completed his doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

Francis Vincent Tiso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, he was a teaching assistant at Columbia and teaches Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University.

Francis Wilford was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He served as a fellow member at The Asiatic Society (~1784–1822) and was Secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth and Harvard, as well as under Paul Pelliot, and served as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar educated at Fordham and the University of Chicago. He was a professor at Boston College (1984–2005) before joining Harvard University in 2005 as Parkman Professor of Divinity.
Francisco García Ayuso was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Munich under Martin Haug from approximately 1870 to 1872.

Francisco Varela worked in philosophy and cognitive neuroscience, holding degrees from the University of Chile and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Chile, CNRS, and the Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital (~1988–2001), and co-founded the Mind and Life Institute.

Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history. Educated at Hamburg, Oxford, and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper, he taught at EPHE and Columbia before serving as Director of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient from 1991 to 2021.

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and was supervised by Stewart Sutherland, also studying under Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, and others.

Frank Lee Woodward was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his BA and MA at Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, and studied under Caroline Rhys Davids. He served as principal of Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translated for the Pali Text Society.

Frank Raymond Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at SOAS under Kenneth de Burgh Codrington. He taught at SOAS (1954–1959) and held a lectureship and readership in Indian Studies at the University of Cambridge from 1959 to 1989.

Frank-Richard Hamm specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate under Walther Schubring at the University of Hamburg, where he taught (1948–1952, 1957–1964), before becoming a professor at the University of Bonn in 1965.

Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. under Maurice Bloomfield at Johns Hopkins. He was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale (1926–1953).

Franz Altheim was a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1919–1928), he held posts there (~1928–1943), at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1943–1950), and at the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1964).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen and habilitated at Frankfurt. From 1966 to 1971, he was a professor and seminar director at the University of Hamburg.

Franz Boas was a linguist and anthropologist educated at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, who also studied under Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark University, the American Museum of Natural History, and Columbia University (~1896–1942).

Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Paris under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. From 1821 to 1867, he held the Chair of Sanskrit at the Humboldt University of Berlin.

Franz Heinrich Trithen was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp at the Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the British Museum (~1844–1848) and was Professor of Modern Languages at the University of Oxford from 1848 to 1854.

Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Deccan College (1866–1881) before holding the chair of Indology at Göttingen from 1881.
